title: The Log-Concave and kappa-Concave Steinhaus-Trybula Barriers: Tangent Stochastic Dominance, Quantile Phase Transitions, and Convolution Transitivity
abstract: In the classical Steinhaus-Trybula paradox, n independent real random variables can form a non-transitive cycle X_1 > X_2 > ... > X_n > X_1 with pairwise win probabilities approaching the Usiskin spectrum 1 - 1/(4 cos^2(pi/(n+2))), rising from the golden ratio (sqrt(5)-1)/2 ~ 0.6180 at n=3 to 3/4 as n -> infinity. We uncover a sharp geometric dichotomy between unimodality and convexity: while unimodal (even C^infinity) random variables suffer zero penalty and achieve the entire Usiskin spectrum up to 3/4, Borell kappa-concavity imposes universal, size-independent ceilings across all cycle lengths and all non-acyclic tournaments. Using a five-line Tangent Stochastic Dominance Lemma for kappa-concave survival functions, we establish exact sharp median-crossing and tournament barriers: M(1) = 1/2 (uniforms, strict transitivity), M(1/2) = (13 - 8*sqrt(2))/3 ~ 0.5621 (2D convex body projections / concave densities), M(0) = (1 + 2*ln 2)/4 ~ 0.5966 (all log-concave variables, strictly beating both Grunbaum's 1 - 1/e ~ 0.6321 and Trybula's 3-variable golden ratio for every n >= 3), and M(-1) = 1/2 + (ln 3)/8 ~ 0.6373 (Cauchy-tail Pareto), smoothly bridging 1/2 to 3/4 and crossing the golden ratio at kappa_* ~ -0.4508. For log-concave variables at arbitrary quantile q in (0, 1), we prove an exact phase transition at q_* = 1 - exp(-lambda_*) ~ 0.7153 ((1 + 2*lambda_*) exp(-lambda_*) = 1) from equal-scale symmetry to scale collapse, yielding the exact point-mass cycle capacity 1 - exp(-lambda_3) ~ 0.5401. Via 1D localization we reduce tau_LC(C_n) to truncated exponentials and derive exact two-sided and one-sided exponential chain limits p_Exp^* ~ 0.5491 and p_Exp^+ ~ 0.5195. Finally, we prove that under k-fold i.i.d. convolution, every finite log-concave family collapses asymptotically to the transitive lexicographic order of its alternating odd cumulants (kappa_1, -kappa_3, +kappa_5, ...). The core algebraic, rational-bracket, inductive, and parity lemmas (10 theorems) are certified in Lean 4.36.0.
